## Configure

Use environment variables or pass values directly.

To get an API key, log in to `https://console.gmicloud.ai/`. In the **Compute** panel, open **Access** → **API Keys** and click **Create API key**.

```bash theme={null}
export GMI_SANDBOX_API_KEY="your-api-key"
```

Set `GMI_SANDBOX_IDC_NAME` (or pass `idc_name`) to choose the IDC for creating sandboxes and templates and for listing product specifications. Sandbox and template creation fall back to your organization's default IDC when neither is set (400 `idc_name is required` if it has none); listing product specifications always needs an IDC:

```bash theme={null}
export GMI_SANDBOX_IDC_NAME="us-central-iowa16"
```
results.title: Configure

results.excerpt:
To maintain system stability and equitable access, our API enforces rate limiting, controlling how frequently an organization can send requests within a certain time window.

API rate limits are defined in two ways:

* **TPM (Tokens per Minute)** for LLM models
* **RPH (Requests per Hour)** for video models

These limits are enforced at the organization level.
results.title: Rate limits

results.excerpt:
## Limits

| Item              | Current behavior                                                      | What to do                                                                      |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sandbox start     | A new sandbox is `pending` for a short time before `running`          | Call `wait_until_running` before commands or file transfers                     |
| Default lifetime  | 24 hours if `timeout_seconds` is not set                              | Set `timeout_seconds` in tests; adjust with `set_timeout`                       |
| Command wait      | A synchronous `execute` waits at most 25 seconds                      | Use `wait=False` and poll with `get_execution`                                  |
| Command output    | `stdout` and `stderr` each return at most 1 MiB                       | Write output to a file and download it                                          |
| Upload size       | About 500 MB per upload; larger returns 413                           | Split the file, or download it from ins [truncated]

results.excerpt:
Create an API key
Allows a user to generate an API key for their organization.

REST Endpoint POST /organizations/{orgId}/api-keys
Summary: Create an API key
Description: Allows a user to generate an API key for their organization.
Path parameters:
- orgId: type string<uuid>; required; description The organization's ID.
- Must be a valid UUID.

Request body:
Description: The API key creation request.
Content type: application/json
- name: type string; required; description The API key name.
- scope: type enum<string>; description The API key scope. Default value is `ie_model`.; enum ie_model, ce_resource
- expiresAt: type integer; description The UNIX timestamp when API key will expire (UTC).
- Must be a UNIX timestamp in seconds and must be greater than the current time.
- If not set, the key will not expire.

Responses:
201: Successfully created an API key.
Content type: application/json
- key: type string; required; description The generated API key (returned only once).
400: - [group:**request**, code:**0**]: Invalid field in the request.
- [group:**request**, code:**1**]: The request body is required.
- [group:**api-key**, code:**0**]: The organization has reached the maximum [truncated]

**Model ID**

```bash theme={null}
GMI-MiniMeTalks-Workflow
```

**Calling method:** async

MiniMeTalks combines Seedream 4.0 and WAN 2.5 in a two-stage AI pipeline to create lively, music-synchronized mini avatars. In Step 1, Seedream 4.0 builds a cohesive 3D “bottle world,” blending uploaded portraits into a realistic miniature avatar with consistent lighting and perspective. In Step 2, WAN 2.5 animates the avatar with lip-sync, expressive motion, and rhythm-based choreography, matching the tone and beat of the selected music.The workflow supports customizable duration, cinematic 768 P output, and is ideal for personalized digital performances, creative storytelling, and social sharing.

results.excerpt: Video models cover text-to-video, image-to-video, reference-guided generation, editing, avatars, and post-processing. Check each model for supported resolutions, durations, and control inputs (first/last frame, reference video, etc.).
results.title: Video Models

results.excerpt:
## Capabilities & limits (public preview)

* Duration: 3-10s (1s increments) or `auto`; Resolution: 720p; Aspect ratio: `auto`, 16:9 or 9:16
* With a `video` input the output follows the source clip — set `durationSeconds` to `auto` (or omit it); an explicit duration that doesn't match the source is rejected by the model
* Up to 5 reference images; input video up to 10s
* Not yet supported: audio references, last-frame guidance, scene extension
results.title: Capabilities & limits (public preview)

results.excerpt:
## Video Specifications

* **Duration**: 5-10 seconds
* **Resolution**: Fixed at 480P (832x480)
* **Quality**: Excellent quality optimized for fast generation
